event.description:
[vc_row type=”in_container” full_screen_row_position=”middle” column_margin=”default” column_direction=”default” column_direction_tablet=”default” column_direction_phone=”default” scene_position=”center” text_color=”dark” text_align=”left” row_border_radius=”none” row_border_radius_applies=”bg” row_position_desktop=”default” row_position_tablet=”inherit” row_position_phone=”inherit” overflow=”visible” overlay_strength=”0.3″ gradient_direction=”left_to_right” shape_divider_position=”bottom” bg_image_animation=”none”][vc_column column_padding=”no-extra-padding” column_padding_tablet=”inherit” column_padding_phone=”inherit” column_padding_position=”all” flex_gap_desktop=”10px” column_element_direction_desktop=”default” column_element_spacing=”default” desktop_text_alignment=”default” tablet_text_alignment=”default” phone_text_alignment=”default” background_color_opacity=”1″ background_hover_color_opacity=”1″ column_backdrop_filter=”none” column_shadow=”none” column_border_radius=”none” column_link_target=”_self” column_position=”default” gradient_direction=”left_to_right” overlay_strength=”0.3″ width=”1/1″ tablet_width_inherit=”default” animation_type=”default” bg_image_animation=”none” border_type=”simple” column_border_width=”none” column_border_style=”solid”][vc_column_text css=”” text_direction=”default”]

Columbia, SC – September 14, 2026 – One Columbia Arts and Culture is opening its doors this Hispanic Heritage Month for “Puentes del Arte,” a free community Open House celebrating the richness of Hispanic culture through art, music, and food. The event takes place Thursday, October 1, from 6-8 PM at 801 Wildwood Avenue, Columbia, SC 29203.

“Puentes del Arte” means “Bridges of Art,” and that’s exactly the spirit One Columbia hopes to capture: connection, celebration, and community, all built around creativity. Guests can look forward to an evening full of color and rhythm, with live music from David Rodriguez and The Latin Hustle setting the tone for the night.

Attendees will also have the opportunity to view art through a collaboration with Palmetto Luna Arts, a local organization dedicated to promoting Latino arts and culture in the Midlands. And no celebration is complete without great food. Takosushi will be on-site serving up its signature flavors, adding one more layer of cultural connection to the evening.

“Last year, we hosted our first open house at the Keenan House, and it was a tremendous success. Our goal was simple: to create a welcoming space for community and connection while reintroducing people to One Columbia,” said Xavier Blake, Executive Director of One Columbia Arts and Culture. “As we began planning this year’s event, we asked ourselves how we could be even more intentional. Our board had the wonderful idea of celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month in partnership with Limitless Community Development and from that vision, Puentes del Arte was born. This year’s open house will serve as a special kickoff to Carnaval del Barrio, taking place Saturday, October 3, from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Finlay Park. Carnaval del Barrio is another incredible event celebrating the Hispanic cultures, creativity, and community that enrich our city. We look forward to celebrating with you in October!”

Tanya Rodriguez-Hodges, Executive Director of Limitless Community Development, echoed that spirit of unity: “Celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month is about more than honoring culture; it is about opening our hearts to one another, learning from our neighbors, and creating a community where everyone feels welcome. We are grateful to partner with One Columbia Arts and Culture on Puentes del Arte and invite people from every background to experience the beauty, creativity, and traditions of Hispanic heritage. This meaningful evening will lead into Carnaval del Barrio, a free community celebration on Saturday, October 3, from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Finlay Park. Together, these events remind us that when we share our stories and celebrate our cultures, we build stronger bridges and bring our communities closer together.”

Whether you’re an art enthusiast, a longtime supporter of multicultural events, or simply looking for a fun night out in Columbia, “Puentes del Arte” offers something for everyone. It’s a chance to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month in a way that feels personal, artistic, and deeply rooted in community.

The event is free and open to the public. RSVPs can be made through Eventbrite at eventbrite.com/e/open-house-puentes-del-arte-tickets-2001007493278, so guests can simply show up ready to enjoy the music, art, and food.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

event.description:
[vc_row type=”in_container” full_screen_row_position=”middle” column_margin=”default” column_direction=”default” column_direction_tablet=”default” column_direction_phone=”default” scene_position=”center” text_color=”dark” text_align=”left” row_border_radius=”none” row_border_radius_applies=”bg” row_position_desktop=”default” row_position_tablet=”inherit” row_position_phone=”inherit” overflow=”visible” overlay_strength=”0.3″ gradient_direction=”left_to_right” shape_divider_position=”bottom” bg_image_animation=”none”][vc_column column_padding=”no-extra-padding” column_padding_tablet=”inherit” column_padding_phone=”inherit” column_padding_position=”all” flex_gap_desktop=”10px” column_element_direction_desktop=”default” column_element_spacing=”default” desktop_text_alignment=”default” tablet_text_alignment=”default” phone_text_alignment=”default” background_color_opacity=”1″ background_hover_color_opacity=”1″ column_backdrop_filter=”none” column_shadow=”none” column_border_radius=”none” column_link_target=”_self” column_position=”default” gradient_direction=”left_to_right” overlay_strength=”0.3″ width=”1/1″ tablet_width_inherit=”default” animation_type=”default” bg_image_animation=”none” border_type=”simple” column_border_width=”none” column_border_style=”solid”][vc_column_text css=”” text_direction=”default”]Carnaval del Barrio Returns to Columbia for a Celebration of Latino Culture, Music, and Community

Limitless Community Development is proud to announce the return of Carnaval del Barrio, one of the Midlands’ largest celebrations of Hispanic Heritage month, on Saturday, October 3, 2026, at Finlay Park in downtown Columbia with free entry.

Limitless Community Development is honored to recognize Wells Fargo Bank as the Premier Sponsor of Carnaval del Barrio 2026. Their generous support will help make this year’s celebration possible and expand access to an inclusive cultural experience for families throughout South Carolina.

Drawing hundreds of attendees each year, Carnaval del Barrio is a family-friendly festival that celebrates the rich traditions, diversity, and contributions of the diverse Hispanic community through live entertainment, authentic cuisine, cultural performances, local artisans, community resources, and interactive activities for all ages.
Hosted by Limitless Community Development, the festival serves as more than a cultural celebration, it is an opportunity to bring communities together, support local businesses, and connect families with valuable community resources in an inclusive and welcoming environment.

“Carnaval del Barrio is more than a festival, it is a celebration of our community’s rich cultural heritage and an opportunity to bring people together through music, art, food, and shared experiences. Each year, we strive to create an inclusive event where every family feels welcomed, connected, and proud to celebrate the diversity that makes our community so special,” said Tanya Rodriguez-Hodges, Executive Director of Limitless Community Development.

Festival attendees can enjoy:
• Free Entry
• Live music by local artists DJ Angel, Los Del 9-54, David Rodriguez, and Latin Hustle
• Live musical performances by international artists MXKA and Bella Dose
• Cultural Dance performances
• A variety of food vendors
• Artisan and marketplace vendors
• Community resource organizations
• Family-friendly activities

As one of the premier cultural events held at Finlay Park, Carnaval del Barrio continues to strengthen community connections while celebrating the vibrant traditions and diversity of the community throughout South Carolina.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

event.description:
The Koger Center for the Arts has set the headliners for the first Levitt AMP Columbia Music Series, a series of free outdoor concerts sponsored in part by the Levitt Foundation. The concerts will take place on the Plaza Stage on the Koger Center’s front lawn from 5:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m., with the rain location being indoors in either the Black Box Theater or second floor lobby.

The Levitt AMP Columbia Music Series is dedicated to uplifting Columbia as a cultural hub and destination for accessible entertainment. The series is supported by a variety of community partners, including the Jasper Project, ONE Columbia, ColaJazz, South Carolina Philharmonic, University of South Carolina Student Life, Black Nerd Mafia, the South Carolina Commission for Community Advancement and Engagement, the Columbia Chamber, the Vista Guild and the City of Columbia.

Geared to towns and cities with populations under 250,000, Levitt AMP grantees reflect the three goals of the LevittAMP Music Series program: Amplify community pride and a city’s unique character; enrich lives through the power of free, live Music; and illustrate the importance of inclusive and vibrant public Places. From rural Alaska to Appalachian Main Streets and Midwestern locales, Levitt AMP is a catalytic opportunity for towns and cities across America to realize a shared mission—building community through music to create a healthy and thriving future for all. Columbia is the only Levitt AMP location in South Carolina.

Columbia residents are encouraged to follow along with the development of the series over the next three years by visiting www.KogerCenterForTheArts.com, and following @LevittAmpColumbia and @KogerCenterForTheArts on Instagram.
